Find, measure and decode what is hidden in a text

Source: R/emoji-hidden.R
emoji_hidden.Rd

emoji_hidden() reports, per row, the code points riding invisibly in a text column that Unicode gives no visible meaning to: runs of variation selectors after an emoji, and tag characters outside a flag. These are the two published ways of smuggling a message through an emoji, invisibly and past copy and paste, into whatever reads the text next, a language model included. The verb counts them, says how many bytes they cost a tokenizer, and decodes the payload when it is in one of the two published encodings.

Usage

emoji_hidden(data, text)

Arguments

data

A data frame or tibble containing a text column. Grouped data frames are accepted. The verbs that work a row at a time (adding columns, or keeping and expanding rows) carry the grouping through to their result, as dplyr::mutate() and dplyr::filter() do. The verbs that pool across rows – the counts, the co-occurrence edge lists, the time series – warn that they ignore the grouping and return one corpus-wide answer.

text

The text column to scan, supplied unquoted. Any atomic column is accepted and read as character, so a factor works and a numeric, Date or logical one simply contains no emoji. A list column – or a data-frame column – is refused rather than coerced, because coercing one deparses it and the emoji found would be in the code rather than in your data. What counts as an emoji is the same in every verb; see the Detection section of tidyEmoji for the one case that surprises people, code points that are emoji only when they carry U+FE0F.

Value

data, as a tibble, with six columns added:

.emoji_n_hidden

the number of hidden code points.

.emoji_hidden_bytes

their size in UTF-8 bytes, which is what a byte-level tokenizer pays for.

.emoji_hidden_kind

"none", "variation_selectors", "tags" or "both".

.emoji_hidden_segments

the number of contiguous runs of hidden code points.

.emoji_hidden_payload

the decoded text, runs joined by " | ", with every control character shown as <U+XXXX>; NA when nothing is hidden or a run is in neither published encoding.

.emoji_hidden_decoded

TRUE when every run decoded, FALSE otherwise, including when nothing is hidden.

A grouped input stays grouped. NA text has nothing hidden.

Details

What counts as hidden is decided by two exact rules from Unicode's own data, not by a guess:

  • A variation selector is hidden when it cannot be part of any sequence Unicode defines: when it follows another selector (no defined sequence has two), when it is an ideographic selector (U+E0100 to U+E01EF) that does not follow a CJK ideograph, or when it is one of U+FE00 to U+FE0D and the pair is not a standardized variation sequence. A single U+FE0E or U+FE0F is never hidden, wherever it stands, because redundant presentation selectors are common in ordinary text and one carries at most one byte.

  • A tag character is hidden unless it is inside a well-formed flag tag sequence: U+1F3F4, tag letters spelling a subdivision code, then U+E007F. The England, Scotland and Wales flags are untouched, and so is a well-formed subdivision flag the catalogue does not list.

So Japanese text spelled with ideographic variation selectors, the mathematical and Mongolian variants Unicode standardizes, every keycap, every catalogue spelling and every flag report nothing. Zero-width spaces, joiners and non-joiners are deliberately not inspected: they are not emoji mechanisms, and Persian, the Indic scripts, Thai and Khmer need them. Use a general Unicode-security tool for those.

Decoding covers the two published encodings only: variation selectors as bytes (U+FE00 to U+FE0F as 0 to 15, U+E0100 to U+E01EF as 16 to 255, the scheme of Butler, 2025), accepted only when the bytes are valid UTF-8; and tag characters U+E0020 to U+E007E as ASCII. Each contiguous run of hidden code points is decoded on its own and the runs are joined by " | ". A row with any run in neither encoding gets an NA payload and .emoji_hidden_decoded = FALSE; it is still counted.

The payload is attacker text, returned as data. Do not paste it into a model. Every C0 and C1 control character and every bidirectional control in it is replaced by a visible <U+XXXX> marker, so printing the result in a console or a knitted report cannot recolour or rewrite the terminal or reorder what a reader sees.

There is no presentation argument, because neither rule depends on it: a U+FE0F after a text-default glyph is valid whatever the caller counts as an emoji. emoji_sanitize() and emoji_to_text() remove these code points by default, under every policy, and emoji_summary() and emoji_token_cost() count them.

References

Butler P (2025). Smuggling arbitrary data through an emoji. https://paulbutler.org/2025/smuggling-arbitrary-data-through-an-emoji/

Hackett W, Birch L, Trawicki S, Suri N, Garraghan P (2025). Bypassing LLM Guardrails: An Empirical Analysis of Evasion Attacks against Prompt Injection and Jailbreak Detection Systems. arXiv:2504.11168.

See also

emoji_sanitize(), whose default hidden = "remove" deletes what this reports; emoji_token_cost() for what the rest of the emoji cost.

Examples

# "hi" hidden after a grinning face, one variation selector per byte
hide <- function(s) {
  b <- as.integer(charToRaw(s))
  intToUtf8(ifelse(b < 16L, 0xFE00L + b, 0xE0100L + b - 16L))
}
df <- data.frame(text = c(paste0("hello \U0001F600", hide("hi")),
                          "plain \U0001F600"))
emoji_hidden(df, text)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 7
#>   text     .emoji_n_hidden .emoji_hidden_bytes .emoji_hidden_kind 
#>   <chr>              <int>               <int> <chr>              
#> 1 hello 😀󠅘󠅙               2                   8 variation_selectors
#> 2 plain 😀               0                   0 none               
#> # ℹ 3 more variables: .emoji_hidden_segments <int>,
#> #   .emoji_hidden_payload <chr>, .emoji_hidden_decoded <lgl>

# the rewriting verbs remove it by default
nchar(emoji_sanitize(df, text)$text)
#> [1] 7 7
nchar(emoji_sanitize(df, text, hidden = "keep")$text)
#> [1] 9 7
